note: Five small primitive camping areas strung along the last 2 km of the gravel entrance road west of the area headquarters, in oak-pine woods: Mill Creek (a gravel pull-off at a bend, the first reached), Long Hollow (a gravel loop), Pine Loop and Little Pine (in pine stands beside the road) and Possum Hollow (an open mown field with a gravel lot opposite the headquarters, beside the shooting range). Three have an accessible privy. The four on the north side of the road are outside the fenced elk refuge, whose gate is at the headquarters and opens in daylight only. About 7 miles of gravel from the end of Route H; the agency warns that Peck Ranch gravel roads may need good ground clearance and can be cut by high water at stream crossings. Spot length is not published. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Designated Camping Sites'/'Individual Campsites' - five named camping areas on the map and five GIS points, all on the entrance road just west of the headquarters. Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. Four of five are outside the elk refuge fence; no closure names a camping area. Pin is on the smallest spot (optional move). PHONE differs from the area page.
flags: PHONE: the area page's 'For more information call' number is (573) 469-0897; stored 417-256-7161 is the Ozark regional office in West Plains printed on the (older) brochure. Suggest 573-469-0897. apply.py does not write phone.

INCLUSION (stays): the page lists 'Camping: Open Camping - Walk-in/Float-in/Backpack', 'Designated Camping Sites' and 'Individual Campsites'; the brochure: 'Primitive camping is permitted in areas designated on the area map.' The 09/13 map names five: Mill Creek Camping Area, Long Hollow Camping Area, Pine Loop Camping Area and Little Pine Camping Area (the last two drawn 'Primitive Camping Area w/ Disabled Accessible Privy') north of the entrance road, and Possum Hollow Camping Area (also with privy) south of the road by the headquarters and shooting range. GIS layer 27 matches, west to east: 402 at 37.04231,-91.20815 (Mill Creek, the stored pin), 1063 at 37.04395,-91.20046 (Long Hollow), 147 at 37.04282,-91.19369 (Pine Loop), 1064 at 37.04267,-91.18785 (Little Pine), 1062 at 37.04162,-91.18608 (Possum Hollow). On leaf-off imagery: Mill Creek is a gravel pull-off ~20 x 15 m at a road bend; Long Hollow a gravel loop ~30 m across with a small building at its head; Pine Loop and Little Pine are short spurs into pine stands (pads hidden by the pines); Possum Hollow an open mown field ~120 x 60 m with a gravel lot, directly across the road from the headquarters. All drive-in; a 23-ft rig fits the pull-off, the loop and the field.

ELK REFUGE / CLOSURES: the map draws the refuge fence along the south side of the entrance road, so Mill Creek, Long Hollow, Pine Loop and Little Pine (north of the road, in the hatched Public Hunting Area) are outside the refuge. Possum Hollow is south of the road at the headquarters, where the map notes 'the entrance to the Refuge is located at the Area Headquarters and is open during daylight hours only'; I could not tell from the map or imagery which side of the gate the field is on. Closures I found apply to the refuge and its driving tour, not to a camping area: elk tours page - 'Driving tours on Peck Ranch Conservation Area will be closed October 11–12, November 5–9, and December 6–7 for managed deer hunts', open 'sunrise to sunset seven days a week — except managed deer hunts, fall firearms deer season, and in the event that roads are closed due to weather', and 1 pm to sunset April 20-May 10; the older brochure - 'The refuge will be closed to the general public during the Managed Deer Hunts as well as a period from April 1 to July 1' (walk-in use only). Neither page says a camping area closes. Season (manual, year-round) left as stored.

ACCESS CAVEAT (not a 4WD rule): MDC's directions are 'From Winona, take Route H east 5 miles, then continue east on gravel 7 miles'. The elk tours page says 'the gravel roads on Peck Ranch may not be accessible to vehicles without adequate ground clearance, and some roads may also be impassible at times due to high water at stream crossings' - written about the tour roads inside the refuge, but it does not exempt the entrance road. I could not check the 7 miles for a low-water crossing: the Overpass mirror did not answer (OSM unread), and nothing on the area page mentions one. Caveat written in the note. QUESTION for AWH: keep with the caveat, as written?

PIN (optional move, 700 m): stored 37.04231,-91.20815 is the Mill Creek pull-off, a real designated spot but the smallest and the farthest from the privies. If a main camp is wanted, Long Hollow's gravel loop at 37.04395,-91.20046 is the clearest RV spot on imagery, and Possum Hollow's field at 37.04162,-91.18608 the largest (beside the shooting range). All five share one road within 2 km - no split.
HORSE CAMP: none labelled on the page, brochure or map. WATERFRONT (stored not waterfront, kept): Mill Creek here is an intermittent headwater stream in timber.
The page gives 29,567 acres (text 29,763); the map and brochure 23,762.
